ideas.title: Multi-leg exits are costed at the flat floor while single-leg exits use the real quote
ideas.thesis: paper_manager._get_spread_slippage charges 30% of the live bid-ask (floor $0.05, cap $0.50) — but only on the single-leg close path (line 1361). The multi-leg path (line 1254) charges a flat slippage_per_share x n_legs regardless of what the structure quotes. MEASURED 2026-07-29 against the archived quotes of the exact contracts logged, on their own entry dates (n=172 contract-days): the flat constant is not uniformly optimistic, it is wrong per structure and in OPPOSITE directions. Bull Put's real half-spread is $0.163 against $0.050 charged (3.2x undercharged); Bear Call's is $0.025 (2x OVERcharged); Iron Condor $0.055 (about right). Re-pricing the closed credit book on that basis flips the ranking: Bull Put +$3,952 -> +$802 (RoR +32.6% -> +6.6%), Bear Call +$571 -> +$1,491 (+9.1% -> +23.8%), book +$4,313 -> +$1,983.
ideas.evidence: src/paper_manager.py:1254 vs :1361. Measurement and re-pricing shipped 2026-07-29 as src/execution_costs.py + scripts/cost_model_report.py. Caveats are printed with the report and are not decorative: the anchor leg's spread is applied to every leg, sample sizes are tens of contract-days from 15 symbols over 19 snapshot dates, and medians say nothing about exiting a loser in a fast market.
ideas.next_step: Do NOT read this as 'Bear Call is better'. The defensible claim is that one flat constant cannot price both structures and the line that looked best was the one it flattered — which means prefer-bull-put-at-small-size rests on a cost assumption its own data contradicts. Before rewiring live exits (which changes the open book), widen the measurement: the archive grows ~1 snapshot/trading day, so re-run the report monthly and see whether the per-structure gap holds at larger n.

ideas.title: Make take-profit thresholds cost-aware by spread width
ideas.thesis: A NFLX $1-wide spread hit its 50%-of-credit take-profit at +56% gross and settled at -1.5% net. Fixed percentage exits ignore what the round trip costs. REFRAMED 2026-07-29: costs are NOT a fixed dollar amount per contract on this broker — commission is US$0. What remains is the bid-ask (measured per structure: $0.163/share Bull Put, $0.025 Bear Call) plus 1.5% currency conversion each way, both proportional to what is traded. So the rule should compare modelled net against the spread being crossed, not against a fixed toll.
ideas.evidence: Auto-close log 2026-07-27; cost measurement in multileg-slippage-is-a-flat-floor; Wealthsimple fee schedule verified 2026-07-29.
ideas.next_step: Require modelled net P&L > 0 before a take-profit fires. Note: changes live exit behaviour across the open book and the gate cohort - deliberate decision, not a cleanup. If picked up, coordinate with mark-fallback-hardcoded-vol so both exit-path changes land as one reviewed, journaled change rather than two separate marking-basis shifts.

ideas.title: Hold credit spreads to expiry instead of closing at 50% take-profit
ideas.thesis: Letting an OTM spread expire worthless avoids the closing leg entirely. STRENGTHENED 2026-07-29 by the real broker schedule: on Wealthsimple, assignment is US$0 and auto-exercise is US$0, so expiry costs nothing at all — the objection this idea was hedging against (assignment risk on ITM-at-expiry) carries no fee, only the position risk. The '$22.60 fixed round trip' framing is retired: commission is US$0, so the round trip is spread plus 1.5% currency conversion each way, both of which are avoided entirely by not trading out.
ideas.evidence: docs/PROFITABILITY_FINDINGS.md section 7; Wealthsimple fee schedule verified 2026-07-29 (options commission US$0, contract fee US$0, assignment US$0, auto-exercise US$0). Mechanism behind the NFLX +56% gross / -1.5% net exit.
ideas.next_step: The hazard is not the fee, and the fee is not assignment. Being assigned costs $0; so does auto-exercise. The US$45 is charged only for INSTRUCTIONS the operator issues — an early exercise, or a do-not-exercise to block an automatic one. The scenario that matters is a spread that finishes PARTIALLY in the money: short leg assigned (free), long leg expired worthless, leaving an unhedged 100-share position worth multiples of the account. The $45 is then the cost of escaping it, which is trivial next to the position itself. So the rule is 'hold to expiry, but never sit in the partial-ITM zone into the close'. Quantify how often the short strike is breached while the long strike is not, in the final days, before changing any exit rule.

ideas.title: Prefer Bull Put over Bear Call purely on cost ratio at small size
ideas.thesis: Median Bull Put credit is $122.50 vs Bear Call $47.50. The same fixed $22.60 round-trip is 18% vs 48% of max profit. Nothing to do with edge - it is credit-per-trade against a fixed toll. CONTRADICTED 2026-07-29: the toll is not fixed. It is $0.163/share for Bull Put and $0.025 for Bear Call — measured, not assumed — so the bigger credit comes with a proportionally wider market. Re-priced on real quotes the preference reverses: Bull Put +6.6% return on risk, Bear Call +23.8%. The whole argument was an artifact of costing both structures at the same flat constant.
ideas.evidence: docs/PROFITABILITY_FINDINGS.md section 7, n=159 credit spreads; superseded by scripts/cost_model_report.py and the measurement in multileg-slippage-is-a-flat-floor.
ideas.next_step: Do not act on either direction yet — the reversal rests on 28 Bull Put and 39 Bear Call contract-days. What is already safe to conclude is that 'fixed toll vs bigger credit' is the wrong frame: cost scales with the market you are crossing, so compare structures on measured cost per structure or not at all.

ideas.thesis: Wealthsimple's US$0 contract fee covers equity and ETF options only. Index options are charged: SPX and SPXW US$1.00 per contract, VIX US$1.00, RUT/RUTW US$0.50, XSP US$0.25. config.paper_trading.commission_per_contract is a single number and now reads 0.0, so any index-option result the system produces understates its cost. Today this is latent rather than live — the ledger trades SPY, QQQ and IWM, which are ETFs and genuinely free — but index-put-spread-capacity is an active idea and SPX is the natural venue for it.
ideas.next_step: Before any SPX work, make the commission lookup per-symbol rather than a single constant. A $1/contract fee on a 2-leg vertical is $4 round trip, which is small against SPX-sized credits but is not zero and must not be assumed away by a config field that cannot express it.

ideas.title: UOA cannot be validated — no source pairs open interest with history
ideas.thesis: UOA is built on open-interest deltas between chain snapshots (uoa.py oi_deltas). Validating it needs point-in-time OI, and nothing available has it: dolt_chain carries 7 years of EOD chains with full Greeks but NO open-interest or volume column, while chain_archive.db has OI across only 19 snapshot dates (2026-06-10 to 2026-07-27). The one source with history cannot express the signal; the one that can has no history. For scale, the squeeze study needed 205 settlement dates and 480,744 observations to resolve a ~3pp effect.
ideas.next_step: Do nothing and let chain_archive.db accumulate (~1 snapshot/trading day, testable in roughly a year). Optionally widen it by pulling OCC's free daily volume/OI-by-series files, which cover the whole market rather than just scanned symbols. Do NOT buy a tick-data vendor for this: OPRA carries trades and quotes, not OI, so Databento/dxFeed-class feeds do not contain the field. If buying, the sellers of historical EOD options WITH OI are CBOE DataShop (pay-per-dataset), ORATS (subscription) and OptionMetrics IvyDB (institutional, free via university WRDS). Verify current pricing directly.

ideas.title: The gate constraint is time, not data — no vendor sells a fix
ideas.thesis: When considering spending money on data, note the actual binding constraint: the Long Call cohort needs roughly n=600 to resolve and fills a handful per day. That is a calendar problem. Every dataset purchase considered so far addresses signals that are display-only, while the thing gating real money is sample accumulation.
ideas.evidence: project gate notes; ds feeder logs 5 LC/day.
ideas.next_step: Before any data purchase, ask whether it shortens the gate or only enriches a display layer. So far the answer has been the latter every time. AMENDED 2026-07-30: the calendar problem is also why the gate-redesign (rank IC, terminal conditions, short-premium cohort) matters more than any data acquisition — the cheapest way to shorten the wait is to measure the right thing on the samples already accruing.

ideas.title: Squeeze SETUP is easier to reach live than in the backtest that calibrated it
ideas.thesis: The backtest panel has no options history, so iv_skew is always None and the call-skew leg never scores: max 5 points there. Live, skew is available and the max is 6. SETUP_MIN_POINTS=3 was rescaled against the 5-point budget, which means live SETUP fires on strictly more configurations than the +4.73pp measurement covers. This is the exact mirror of the bug that produced 18 SETUP rows in 480,744 — a threshold calibrated against one point budget and applied to another.
ideas.evidence: src/squeeze/backtest/panel.py passes iv_skew=None; backtest report prints 'iv_skew: unavailable'. detector.py SETUP_MIN_POINTS=3, live max 6 vs backtest max 5.
ideas.next_step: Measure live SETUP frequency against the backtest's SETUP rate on the same universe. If live fires materially more often, either raise the live threshold to 4, or stop scoring skew until it can be validated — an unvalidated +1 is what the whole 2026-07-28 rescoring was meant to remove.

ideas.title: Widen the outlook universe — 16 instruments is the resolution floor
ideas.thesis: The outlook z-scores cross-sectionally across 16 ETFs and rebalances every 21 days, giving ~83 observations. That is why the reversal_1m question came back 'indistinguishable' rather than answered: the study cannot resolve IC differences of ~0.01. Widening the universe helps twice — more names make each cross-sectional z-score less noisy, and more rebalance rows raise the power of every future factor test.
ideas.evidence: DEFAULT_UNIVERSE is 16 tickers; run_backtest reported n=83 (42d) and n=82 (63d) rebalances over 2,037 aligned bars.
ideas.next_step: Add liquid sector/industry ETFs with long histories (aiming for 30-40 names) and re-run the existing backtest to confirm the headline IC survives the wider universe before trusting it for factor tests. Widening must not be assumed free — it changes what the z-scores mean.

Today the mitigation is tribal knowledge ('quit the idle launcher') - a beta tester WILL leave the menu open and then report the tool as unusably slow, and nothing in the product will tell them why. VERIFIED: closing drops the -wal and -shm sidecars, a subsequent read revives them. HOWEVER the 20-50x slowdown itself was NOT reproduced: a local contention benchmark measured holding the connection open as 5x FASTER than releasing it (0.020s vs 0.104s for 300 connect+read in a second process), because a released db recreates its sidecars per connection. So this ships on handle-hygiene grounds and must NOT be described as a proven fix. CORRECTED 2026-07-31 after re-reading the original diagnosis: the naive benchmark was the WRONG TEST, not evidence the fix is wrong. The real mechanism is that an idle launcher holds ~41 handles to tkr-tz.db and a WAL cannot CHECKPOINT while a reader is alive, so it grows unbounded and every concurrent connection re-scans it under lock contention (stack in sqlite3PagerSharedLock, no ESTABLISHED socket; a -ds window went 2m22s -> 55 min with a day-old launcher open). The benchmark used one handle and a tiny WAL, reproducing neither condition. Closing the handles is exactly what lets the WAL truncate, so the fix targets the diagnosed mechanism. iCloud is a DEAD END already chased twice - a synced vs /private/tmp read timed identical (0.005s both); do not chase it again. STILL OUTSTANDING: end-to-end confirmation on the operator's machine (idle for hours, then time a concurrent scan with and without the release). See docs/IDLE_CACHE_RELEASE.md.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: Fix at the source, not with docs. Options in preference order: (1) release/close the shared yfinance session and any sqlite handles (tz-cache, yf_disk_cache.db) whenever the process is idle at a menu prompt, reacquiring lazily on the next action - the menus are the natural release points; (2) if the handle is held inside yfinance internals and cannot be released cleanly, have the menu loop detect >N minutes idle and print a prominent 'this open session is slowing other scans' warning; (3) investigate whether the tz-cache can be opened read-only or with a non-WAL journal mode for our access pattern. shipped.title: A USD account may pay for itself against the 1.5% conversion spread
shipped.thesis: Trading US-listed options from a CAD account converts currency both ways at Wealthsimple's 1.5% spread (below US$10k of conversions; 1.0% to $25k, 0.5% to $100k, 0% above). Nothing in this repo modelled that until now, and it is the largest remaining cost in the book once commissions are correctly set to zero: $1,098 of conversion across 187 closed credit trades in the cohort window alone. A USD account removes it for $10/month.
shipped.evidence: Wealthsimple fee schedule verified 2026-07-29; scripts/cost_model_report.py prints the conversion total. Note the cost scales with money moved, not contract count, so it cannot be traded around by using fewer legs.

There is no per-trade CAD->USD conversion spread to model. The US$10/month subscription is a FIXED cost and is deliberately NOT folded into per-trade friction — it does not scale with activity and would distort a per-trade number — but it is real: at zero trading it is pure overhead, and the break-even against the old 1.5% is roughly US$8k/yr of conversions. For scale, the cohort window alone carried $1,098 of conversion across 187 closed credit trades, so at the book's historical activity the subscription pays for itself many times over. The two open questions this entry used to carry (whether tiering was per-transaction or cumulative, and whether idle USD cash goes uninvested) are now MOOT for the conversion decision, though the idle-cash question still applies to however much USD is held. Revert fx_conversion_rate to 0.015 if the subscription lapses.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: Check actual annual conversion volume rather than this window's, then decide. Two things to confirm first, because both change the answer: whether the tiered rate is assessed on cumulative annual conversions or per transaction, and whether holding USD in the account leaves idle cash uninvested in a way that costs more than the spread saves. shipped.title: The gate reads Pearson IC on skewed option returns - rank IC says the edge is zero
shipped.thesis: Long-call returns are floored at -100% and unbounded above, so Pearson IC is dominated by a handful of +100% take-profit outliers. Checkpoint 2026-07-29 (n=70): Pearson +0.048 (p=0.690) drives an EXTEND, while Spearman is -0.020 (p=0.873) - the two statistics disagree in SIGN, and the bootstrap CI is [-0.175, +0.248]. Rank IC is the industry standard for exactly this distribution shape. src/phase1_checkpoint.py already computes Spearman on line 131; the decision block (lines 135-144) reads only ic_p. Under rank IC the current state is not 'positive but below the bar', it is 'no forward information detected'. This is the single most decision-relevant number in the repo and it is currently flattering the system.
shipped.evidence: reports/checkpoint_2026-07-29.md; reports/checkpoint_history.tsv shows the Pearson IC decaying monotonically as n grows (0.22 at n=4, 0.20 at n=23, 0.11 at n=43, 0.048 at n=70) - the classic signature of an effect that was never there.
shipped.next_step:
SIGNED OFF AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (commit 391e47f). The gate now decides on the SPEARMAN rank IC. config.gate.version = 2; decide_v1 is preserved verbatim and both verdicts print on every checkpoint and in GATE_STATUS.md, because a superseded rule that vanishes cannot be audited. A sign-agreement guard withholds READY whenever rank and Pearson disagree in sign. OUTCOME AT n=92: both rules say STOP (Pearson -0.065, Spearman -0.132, posterior 4%). The redesign did not rescue the long call — it reached the same verdict on a sounder statistic and showed its working.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: AMENDED 2026-07-31: the reporting half SHIPPED (commit 49edfd1/a8acd83) - checkpoint markdown, GATE_STATUS.md, checkpoint_history.tsv (new spearman/p_spearman columns, append-only) and the evidence banner now all render Pearson and Spearman side by side, with an explicit sign-disagreement line. The DECISION half is written up but NOT applied: see docs/GATE_REDESIGN_SPEC.md, which is a draft awaiting the operator's sign-off block. The decision function still reads Pearson, byte-identical, pinned by a regression test. NOTE the cohort has since grown to n=92 with Pearson -0.065, so the next real checkpoint reads STOP under the UNCHANGED rules - the redesign is now urgent rather than theoretical.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: Write the gate-redesign spec (one spec covering this entry, fix-gate-power-math, and repoint-gate-credit - they are one decision). Proposal: decision reads Spearman, or requires Pearson AND Spearman to agree in sign with Spearman clearing the bar. Immediately (allowed without sign-off): render both statistics side-by-side in the checkpoint markdown, the evidence banner, and TRACK_RECORD.md so the operator sees the disagreement every week. Then apply the decision change only on operator approval per DECISIONS.md.
shipped.acceptance: Checkpoint markdown and evidence banner show both statistics; a signed-off spec exists in docs/; the decision function's statistic matches the spec; scripts/test.sh green.

shipped.title: Fix the gate's incoherent power math - and give EXTEND a terminal condition
shipped.thesis: READY needs IC>=0.08 AND p<0.05, but proving IC=0.08 at p<0.05 requires n~601. At the n>=50 trigger, p<0.05 demands observed IC~0.286 - 3.6x the stated bar. The gate cannot fire on its own terms. AMENDED 2026-07-30: the mirror problem is that EXTEND has no exit. STOP requires IC<0.03 and READY requires p<0.05, so an IC drifting in the 0.03-0.08 band extends forever - at ~70 trades per 9 weeks, resolving IC~0.05 at p<0.05 needs n~1,500, i.e. years. The explainer text says 'continue gathering for 2 more weeks' but nothing enforces any deadline. The gate currently has three states and one of them is an infinite loop.
shipped.evidence: Fisher-z: n = (1.96/atanh(IC))^2 + 3. docs/PROFITABILITY_FINDINGS.md section 1; src/phase1_checkpoint.py:135-144; checkpoint_history.tsv accrual rate.
shipped.next_step:
SIGNED OFF AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (commit 391e47f). READY is now P(true rank IC >= 0.08) >= 0.85 rather than the incoherent 'IC>=0.08 AND p<0.05' (which demanded an observed IC of ~0.286 at n=50). STOP fires at posterior <= 0.15, at a rank IC below 0.03, or when the EXTEND allowance is spent. EXTEND IS NOW BOUNDED: at most 2 grants of 2 weeks, tracked in config.gate.extensions_used, after which the gate must resolve. Every state has an entry AND an exit; no state is unbounded — tests/test_gate_v2.py pins that, and also demonstrates the old defect (a 0.05 Pearson IC EXTENDs under v1 at week 600).

PRIOR NEXT STEP: AMENDED 2026-07-31: specced, not applied. docs/GATE_REDESIGN_SPEC.md section 2.3 gives every gate state an entry AND an exit condition, caps EXTEND at 2 grants x 2 weeks, replaces the p-value cliff with posterior bands (READY P>=0.85, STOP P<=0.15) on the already-computed posterior_ic_above, and states all thresholds in effective-n terms (folding in effective-n-in-gate). Awaiting operator sign-off.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: Fold into the gate-redesign spec with gate-statistic-wrong-for-skewed-returns. Proposal to put in front of the operator: (a) EXTEND is granted at most twice (2 weeks each), after which the decision falls to STOP unless the Bayesian posterior P(true IC>=0.08) >= 0.85 (the posterior is already computed and printed, reporting-only, by posterior_ic_above); (b) size the READY test to the effect actually claimed, or switch the claim to one the sample can support. Also fold in effective-n-in-gate (design effect ~1.23 from clustered entries).
shipped.acceptance: The spec enumerates every gate state with an entry AND exit condition; no state is unbounded; operator sign-off recorded; implementation matches.

shipped.title: Exit decisions can fire off a Black-Scholes mark at a hardcoded 30 vol
shipped.thesis: paper_manager.update_positions marks each leg by fast_info.last_price, falling back to daily close, falling back to american_price(..., 0.30) - a model price at sigma=0.30 regardless of the name (src/paper_manager.py:1205). Marking an 80-IV name at 30 vol misprices it severely, and that fabricated mark can TRIGGER a stop-loss or take-profit, i.e. write a permanent exit into the ledger the gate then reads. Separately, preferring last_price over bid/ask mid means marks can be hours stale on illiquid contracts - inconsistent with the repo's own quote-freshness philosophy, and the single-leg close path already knows how to read the live spread (_get_spread_slippage, line ~1361).
shipped.evidence: src/paper_manager.py:1181-1212 (fetch chain: last_price -> 1d close -> american_price at 0.30); schema v16 stores entry IV per row.
shipped.next_step:
SIGNED OFF AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (commit see git log). Spec docs/MARK_TRUSTWORTHINESS_SPEC.md implemented: model-fallback sigma comes from the row's stored entry_iv, a model-sourced mark can never fire an exit, and bid/ask mid is preferred over a stale last trade. Expiry settlement is unaffected and remains the guarantee that no row hangs OPEN forever.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: AMENDED 2026-07-31: specced, NOT implemented - it changes live exit behaviour, so per the exit-rules constraint it needs sign-off first. docs/MARK_TRUSTWORTHINESS_SPEC.md covers all three parts as one decision (entry-IV fallback sigma, model-fallback marks may never fire an exit, bid/ask mid preferred over stale last trade), plus the test plan and the calibration-journal requirement.

PRIOR NEXT STEP: Three changes, one entry, because they all define 'what is a trustworthy mark': (1) the model-price fallback uses the row's stored entry IV (schema has it) instead of 0.30; (2) a mark that came from the model fallback may update unrealized P&L display but must NEVER fire an exit - skip the exit check for that leg that run and log it; (3) prefer bid/ask mid over last trade when both are available, keeping last_price as fallback. This changes live exit behaviour - per the constraints, write it up and get operator sign-off before merging, and note in the calibration journal that post-change exits are on a different marking basis.
shipped.acceptance: No exit can be recorded from a model-fallback mark (test asserts it); fallback sigma comes from the row; mid preferred over last; scripts/test.sh green; operator sign-off recorded.

dead.title: Backtest the credit lines on the Dolt chains instead of waiting a year for them
dead.thesis: gate-is-time-not-data says the binding constraint is calendar, not data — but that is only true for signals nothing historical can express. Bull Put and Bear Call CAN be expressed historically: data/dolt_options.db carries 595,074 chain rows with bid, ask and full Greeks, ~740 dense dates from 2022-01 to 2026-06, with strikes spanning roughly 0.02-0.97 delta. That is enough to construct verticals with real quotes and measure the two lines that carry the book, on data already sitting on disk, without waiting for live accrual.
dead.evidence: RUN 2026-07-29, docs/DOLT_CREDIT_SPREADS.md. 208 weekly entries x 8 megacaps, 2022-2025, real bid/ask crossed, ledger's own exit rules and intrinsic settlement. Bull Put n=1,528 win 66.6% mean -1.89% on max risk; Bear Call n=1,517 win 61.9% mean -2.95%. Both negative even with commissions at the configured US$0 and no FX charged. 29 full max-risk losses (1.9% of trades) carry two thirds of the damage.
dead.next_step: CLOSED on the pre-committed condition: the corpus cannot answer the question that was asked. Mean max risk is $1,753-$1,812 against a live median of $54 (Bear Call) and $128 (Bull Put) — 14-32x the structures actually traded — and 52% of positions were quoted on at most one day, so for half the sample the exit rules under test never ran. Reporting these as validation of the live lines would be the 'number that looks like validation' this entry warned against. The one usable negative to keep: wide megacap credit spreads under this book's exit rules lost money on capital at risk with zero commissions, which is worth knowing before anyone widens the live structures toward these sizes on the intuition that width means safety. The gate-shortening ambition fails on its own terms; see gate-is-time-not-data, which stands.

Within strategy it predicts nothing, and in Short Put it is significantly backwards (-0.305, p=0.007).
